thread:
Maria: Morning — noticed a 1.8x 99p tail for TP all-reduce around 03:42 UTC. Only seen on KV-prefill-heavy workloads where fragments are tiny. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/18625 :eyes:

Samir: Same fleet as the microkernel rollout yesterday? Or driver/infra churn?

Maria: No infra churn. We landed a kernel-selection heuristic tweak + shortened micro-batch coalescing to reduce peak memory. Suspect message-size distribution changed.

Jin: I ran a short repro. TL;DR: ring is winning too often for very small msg sizes. Tree performs better under ~48KB. Numbers from local loopback perf: 
```
TP=4 | msg=16KB | ring: 2.8ms | tree: 1.6ms
TP=4 | msg=64KB | ring: 3.2ms | tree: 4.5ms
```
So the crossover is around ~48KB. Our selector currently biases toward ring because of throughput heuristics.

Devin: Can you paste the exact command to repro in CI container? I can wire a job.

Jin: Reproducer: 
```
./tp_perf --model mock --tp 4 --seq 512 --batch 1 \n  --kv-frag-size=16K --allreduce-algo=auto --repeat 200
```
Minimal nvprof-like snippet: 
```
[0] ncclAllReduce start size=16384 overhead=1.9ms
[1] allreduce kernel launch latency=0.6ms
compute overlap ~12%
```
Small messages show high per-call overhead and poor overlap.

Samir: That matches: when KV prefill emits lots of tiny fragments we end up with many small allreduce ops, so per-op latency dominates. The batching window we recently shortened used to merge those fragments more aggressively.

Maria: Right — the micro-batch change was to lower peak memory for large models, but we may have shifted the msg-size histogram left. Need to avoid regressing latency for small-frag workloads.

Jin: Quick experiment: forcing tree for <=48KB removes the tail in the microbenchmark (99p ~ 45ms -> 23ms). But forcing tree globally hurts large-message throughput.

Devin: Options: A) revert the micro-batch coalescing reduction. B) Tweak kernel selector to prefer tree below threshold (fast mitigation behind flag). C) Smarter adaptive: maintain a per-worker message-size histogram and pick algo per-request.

Samir: Prefer C long-term. B is acceptable short-term as a config flag. A has risk of reintroducing memory spikes. Also add a nightly perf job that simulates KV-prefill small-frag patterns.

Jin: I added a local CI perf job and pushed perf-bot run: https://perf.redwood/bot/18625-run — summary: with tree fallback for <=32KB, 99p tail drops by ~50% on the small-frag test (TP=4).

perf-bot: scheduled nightly regression test for kv-frag-heavy workloads.

Maria: Action items:
- Jin: PR to add selector flag + basic test (ETA: today).
- Devin: CI repro job + console metric (per-node msg-size histogram) (ETA: tomorrow).
- Samir: cost/throughput analysis for reverting vs smarter batching (ETA: Friday).

Jin: I'll scope the selector change to be opt-in behind runtime flag. Also include a small unit test that exercises the crossover threshold.

Devin: For the metric, we should expose: per-TP message-size histogram (buckets: <16K, 16-48K, 48-128K, >128K) + 95/99p allreduce latency. That'll help validate rollout.

Maria: Good. Let's avoid a global force unless the metric shows a persistent shift. Quick mitigation B is fine while Samir assesses batching tradeoffs.

Samir: Also want to check whether kernel selection interacts with quantized kernels. Jin, can you include a small test with int8 kernels in your PR?

Jin: Will do.

Maria: Thanks all — ping me when PRs land. :wave:
